Confirm the defect type, shunt/hemodynamic burden, pulmonary-hypertension classification, and competing congenital or acquired causes before any publication decision.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-25 adds this relationship only as a bounded congenital-shunt association. Atrial septal defects can expose the pulmonary circulation to increased flow and, in selected patients over time, be associated with pulmonary arterial hypertension or pulmonary vascular disease; however, the relationship is heterogeneous and does not apply to every defect or pulmonary-pressure elevation. Require documented atrial septal defect type and size, shunt direction and magnitude, right-heart and pulmonary-pressure findings under accepted clinical criteria, compatible chronology, and congenital-cardiology review. Exclude left-heart disease, lung disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, hypoxia, portal disease, drugs, and other pulmonary-hypertension groups before attributing the association to the defect. Do not infer pulmonary hypertension from an ASD label, dyspnea, or an isolated echocardiographic estimate.
evidenceGaps: Independent congenital-cardiology documentation of atrial septal defect anatomy and pulmonary hypertension
Defect type, shunt fraction, right-heart remodeling, oxygenation, right-heart catheterization or other accepted hemodynamic evidence
Chronology of the defect, shunt burden, pulmonary vascular disease, and any closure or treatment
Classification and exclusion of group 2, group 3, group 4, drug-related, hypoxic, portal, and other pulmonary-hypertension causes

Resolution of publication guard: Require documented ASD anatomy, objective pulmonary hypertension, compatible shunt/chronology, and competing-cause review; do not infer pulmonary hypertension from an ASD label alone.

sourceReferences.citation: Nashat H, Launchedbury R, Abdul-Ghani M, et al. Atrial septal defects and pulmonary arterial hypertension. J Thorac Dis. 2018;10(Suppl 24):S2953-S2965. PMID 30305956. doi:10.21037/jtd.2018.08.92.
sourceReferences.note: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-25 clinical review for the bounded atrial-septal-defect to pulmonary-hypertension proposition. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source remains pending qualified-human review.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 30305956; review of ASD-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension, congenital shunt physiology, and closure considerations; approved ME-25 guard requires objective hemodynamics and pulmonary-hypertension group review.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The cited congenital-cardiology review supports a possible relationship between atrial septal defects and pulmonary arterial hypertension in selected phenotypes, without establishing that every ASD or every pulmonary-hypertension diagnosis has that origin.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established by the current evidence; defect anatomy, hemodynamics, chronology, classification, and alternative pulmonary-hypertension causes require individual review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: An atrial-level left-to-right shunt may increase pulmonary blood flow and vascular stress, with pulmonary vascular remodeling and hypertension possible in selected patients, but the individual hemodynamic pathway remains hypothesized until characterized.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The review addresses ASD-related pulmonary vascular disease but emphasizes heterogeneous anatomy, timing, and pulmonary-hypertension classification rather than an automatic individual pathway.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent ASD and pulmonary-hypertension diagnoses; anatomy and shunt/hemodynamics; chronology; pulmonary-hypertension group classification; and exclusion of left-heart, lung, thromboembolic, hypoxic, portal, drug-related, and other causes.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: left-heart disease or group 2 pulmonary hypertension
connective-tissue or inflammatory pulmonary vascular disease
drug or toxin exposure and other congenital heart disease
